source.version: Research Square preprint v1, posted February 5th, 2026, DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-8774138/v1; not peer reviewed (p. 1 banner)
source.title_on_document: Sequential Human-AI Collaboration Impairs Narrative Creativity in University Students: A Randomized Controlled Trial

supplement.where: Research Square preprint page, 'Supplementary Files' list (p. 20): DataSPSS.sav and researchtools.pdf; Data Availability statement (p. 12) says datasets and materials will be in the supplementary files. No URL printed.
supplement.holds: Participant-level SPSS data (DataSPSS.sav) and the research instruments (researchtools.pdf). The PDF on file gives no arm-level SDs, unadjusted means, or regression tables; participant-level SDs and per-arm ns after exclusions could only come from the data file.

paper_design_summary: 112 undergraduates at Yangzhou University (valid cases after screening) were randomly assigned to four conditions for a two-stage story-writing task ('Imagine and depict the future world', 15 minutes per stage): AI-first (GenAI for the first draft, final draft alone), AI-follow (first draft alone, GenAI for the final draft), AI-parallel (GenAI in both stages), and Human-only (no AI). Ten trained student raters and DeepSeek-V3 scored both drafts on originality, fluency, flexibility, and elaboration (9-point scales); the main analysis is an ANCOVA of final-draft creativity controlling for first-draft creativity and covariates. Creative self-efficacy was also measured by questionnaire.

studies.label: Two-stage narrative writing experiment with four collaboration models

assignment.what_was_assigned: Collaboration model: AI-first, AI-follow, AI-parallel, or Human-only (control)
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of four experimental conditions: (1) AI-first - Human-AI collaboration on the first draft followed by independent refinement (n = 28, 16 male)
assignment.locator: p. 4, Section 2.1 Participants; also p. 6, Section 2.4 Procedure

arms.name: AI-first
arms.description: Human-AI collaboration on the first draft, then independent refinement of the final draft without AI (could reference but not modify the first draft)

arms.name: AI-follow
arms.description: Independent first draft, then human-AI collaboration on the final draft

arms.name: AI-parallel
arms.description: Human-AI collaboration in both the first and the final draft

arms.name: Human-only
arms.description: Independent creation in both stages without any AI tools (control)

participants.exclusions: The 112 are 'valid cases' remaining after 'data screening for attrition and non-compliance'; the number recruited or assigned before screening is not stated (p. 4). Five participants (4.5 percent) had missing values, filled by multiple imputation (MICE, five datasets), keeping N = 112 (p. 7). Influential cases by Cook's distance (D > 4/n) were then dropped model by model: 7 in the human-rated overall analysis (F df 3, 96, implying 105 analyzed), 8 in the AI-rated analysis (F df 3, 95, implying 104), an unstated number in each subdomain analysis, and 10 in the self-efficacy analysis (N = 102) (pp. 7-9). Per-arm counts after these exclusions are not reported.
participants.who: Undergraduate students at Yangzhou University from humanities, social sciences, STEM, agriculture, and medicine; required to have GenAI experience; mean age 19.47 (SD 1.20); recruited December 2024; paid 25 to 45 CNY based on performance
participants.quote: Following data screening for attrition and non-compliance, 112 valid cases remained, resulting in a total of 224 creative writing samples (first and final drafts combined).

ai_tool.name_model: Participant's choice of GenAI tool, e.g., ChatGPT or DeepSeek (not recorded per participant)
ai_tool.how_used: In AI-assisted stages participants could use any GenAI tool, send prompts freely, ask questions, and adopt or reject AI-generated content (pp. 5, 7). Interaction modes were not controlled or categorized (p. 11).

task.description: Open-ended story writing on the prompt 'Imagine and depict the future world'; a first draft and then a final draft. Instructions asked for novelty, idea richness, diverse perspectives, detail, coherence, and structure; compensation rose with rated quality.

outcomes.name: Final-draft overall creativity, human-rated (AI-follow and AI-parallel vs Human-only)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Ten undergraduate raters (completed innovation or entrepreneurship coursework, university-level creative awards), blind to condition, calibrated on 15 narratives; each narrative rated by all ten on originality, fluency, flexibility, elaboration (9-point scales). How the 'overall' score combines dimensions and raters is not stated. ICC (two-way mixed, absolute agreement, average measures) = 0.722, 95% CI [0.48, 0.88] in formal rating. Estimates are adjusted means from an ANCOVA ('residual model') controlling for first-draft score, age, gender, AI literacy, and creative personality, after excluding 7 influential cases.

contrasts.reported: Omnibus F(3, 96) = 9.62, p < .001, eta-squared = .38. Human-only adjusted M = 5.65 (SE = 0.10) vs AI-follow M = 4.81 (SE = 0.10); p < .001, d = -1.41
Human-only adjusted M = 5.65 (SE = 0.10) vs AI-parallel M = 5.17 (SE = 0.10); p = .262, d = -0.33

outcomes.name: Final-draft overall creativity, human-rated (AI-first vs Human-only; final draft written without AI)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same measure and ANCOVA as S1-O1. In the AI-first arm the final draft was written without AI, immediately after an AI-assisted first draft that participants could reference but not modify. The ANCOVA controls for the first-draft score, which in this arm was itself produced with AI.

contrasts.reported: Omnibus F(3, 96) = 9.62, p < .001, eta-squared = .38. Human-only adjusted M = 5.65 (SE = 0.10) vs AI-first M = 4.86 (SE = 0.10); p = .002, d = -0.95

outcomes.name: First-draft overall creativity, human-rated (AI-first and AI-parallel vs Human-only)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same human rating as S1-O1, applied to first drafts. The paper treats the first draft as the 'baseline'/pre-test, although AI-first and AI-parallel participants wrote it with AI. An ANOVA found 'significant differences' at baseline; no F, p, means, or pairwise tests are printed. Only box plots (Figure 1) show the distributions.

contrasts.reported: Figure 1 box plots only: AI-first first-draft median about 4.6 vs Human-only about 5.2 (visual reading). Text: 'Despite random group assignment, significant differences were found at baseline.'
Figure 1 box plots only: AI-parallel first-draft median about 4.7 vs Human-only about 5.2 (visual reading); no pairwise test reported

data_and_code.data_url: Supplementary file DataSPSS.sav on the Research Square preprint page (p. 20); no URL printed

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomly assigned to three GenAI collaboration arms or a no-AI control (p. 4); 112 people analyzed (105 in the main human-rated ANCOVA after 7 Cook's-distance exclusions, implied by F(3, 96)); narratives were rated for creativity by ten blind raters and by DeepSeek-V3. The pre-screening randomized count is not stated.

one_line_finding: Relative to Human-only writing, final-draft human-rated creativity was lower for AI-first (adjusted M 4.86 vs 5.65, d = -0.95, p = .002) and AI-follow (4.81, d = -1.41, p < .001) and not different for AI-parallel (5.17, d = -0.33, p = .262) (p. 8, Section 3.2).
open_questions: Setting not stated (supervised room or online); coded lab_rct on the basis of a recruited, timed, single-university session. Reviewer may prefer online_rct or another code.

The ANCOVA controls for first-draft creativity, which AI-first and AI-parallel participants produced with AI; the 'baseline' is post-treatment for those arms. Should these adjusted contrasts be used, or should unadjusted final-draft means (only available from DataSPSS.sav) be preferred?
The number of participants recruited or randomized before 'attrition and non-compliance' screening is not reported, so attrition by arm is unknown.
The basis of the reported Cohen's d (which SD, adjusted or raw) is not stated.
How the 'overall creativity' score is built from the four dimensions and ten raters is not stated.
notes: Main results are on pp. 8-9 (text only; no results tables). Table 1 (p. 8) gives arm demographics only. Figures 1-5 (pp. 16-20) are box plots: overall human-rated (Fig 1), overall DeepSeek-rated (Fig 2), human-rated subscales (Fig 3), DeepSeek-rated subscales (Fig 4, no tests reported in text; left out of the outcome list), and creative self-efficacy (Fig 5). Creative self-efficacy is a self-report questionnaire (17 items, 4-point scale) and is not listed as an outcome: ANCOVA F(3, 93) = 2.29, p = .083, N = 102 after excluding 10 influential cases (p. 9). The eta-squared subscript glyph does not render in the PDF (p. 8-9); likely partial eta-squared. Covariates in the residual model: pre-test score, age, gender, AI literacy, creative personality (p. 8). Post hoc power .844 (p. 4). Missing data for 5 participants imputed with MICE (p. 7). Human raters were undergraduates with creative awards, coded human_raters rather than expert_raters. The paper calls the study exploratory (p. 4); no preregistration is mentioned. Ethics approval JKY-2024121611 (p. 4).
